jobs.title: Financial Controller
jobs.description:
Lear For You

Lear, a global automotive technology leader in Seating and E-Systems, enables superior in-vehicle experiences for consumers around the world. Our diverse team of talented employees in 38 countries is driven by a commitment to innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. Lear is Making every drive better™ by providing the technology for safer, smarter, and more comfortable journeys. Lear, headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, serves every major automaker in the world and ranks #186 on the Fortune 500. Further information about Lear is available at lear.com, or follow us on Twitter @LearCorporation.

Job description, responsibilities and duties

• Assist the Plant Controller in all aspects of corporate and internal reporting to ensure adherence to timetables, financial integrity and completeness.
• As with all roles within the Finance department, the role will involve financial control testing to ensure SOX compliance.
• Assist in budget and short-term forecast preparation, profit and loss, cashflow and balance sheet.
• Management of key KPIs including Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable aging.
• SOX Testing Reviews and presentation to the Financial Manager.
• Balance Sheet Reconciliation Reviews.
• Calculation and accounting for reserves
• Management and completion of month-end processes including variance analysis.
• Working closely with external auditors for year end and interim audit work.
• Assist with special finance projects and automations

Personality requirements and skills

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
• Minimum 3-5 years of experience in Financial controlling.
• Previous experience in a manufacturing environment; automotive industry experience is highly preferred.
• Proven experience with: Financial reporting and analysis, Budgeting and forecasting, Month-end and year-end closing activities, Balance sheet reconciliations, Cost accounting and inventory accounting, Cash flow management
• Experience with external and internal audits.
• Hands-on experience with SOX compliance or internal controls.

Employee perks, benefits

• Year-end bonus – 13th salary
• Meal allowance
• Anniversary benefit.
• Referral benefit
• Company canteen
• Flexible working hours
• Vitamin package, fruit days every month, Christmas gifts
• Employee coffee
• Financial consultations.

jobs.description:
Lear For You

We work hard for the people who work for us. We champion our teams and foster collaboration, inclusion, respect and excellence. Because we want to be more for you.

A path to a better career. A better future.

Our teams have invented groundbreaking technologies, manufactured millions of products and earned a long list of awards. Year after year, we’re named one of the World’s Most Admired Companies.

They’re the secret to our success—empowered, inventive and inclusive. Passionate about their craft. Driven to succeed. Because we win together.

Job Description

We are seeking a results-driven and experienced Operations Manager to take full responsibility for the manufacturing operations of the Port Elizabeth plant.  The successful candidate will lead plant performance improvement initiatives, foster a high-performance culture and employer leadership teams to consistently achieve operational objectives.  This role requires a dynamic leader who can build strong teamwork across departments, drive continuous improvement and ensure the achievement of key business, quality, safety and productivity targets.

Responsibilities

- Delivering and exceeding the plant's annual budget and financial objectives.

- Ensuring the achievement of quality targets across TRIM and JIT operations within a three-shift manufacturing environment.

- Promoting a world-class safety culture and driving zero lost-time injuries and incidents.

- Achieving MOS efficiency targets for both TRIM and JIT operations.

- Managing headcount plans, labour forecasts, and direct and indirect labour efficiencies.

- Driving plant productivity and operational efficiency while ensuring zero missed units and minimising production disruptions.

- Overseeing engineering projects and ensuring successful execution in line with approved project timelines.

- Achieving inventory targets while eliminating premium freight costs and lost production units.

- Leading plant management and operational teams to deliver forecast volumes and key performance indicators (KPIs).

- Driving Continuous Improvement (CI) initiatives and ensuring targeted cost savings and operational benefits are realised.

- Building and maintaining a unified, accountable, and high-performing management team.

Education Requirements

- Relevant tertiary education such as a National Diploma in Production Management or equivalent qualification.

Experience Requirements

- A minimum of 5 years Operations Management experience within a TRIM and JIT automotive manufacturing environment.

- Proven track record of achieving operational, quality, safety, and financial targets within a manufacturing setting.

-
Strong leadership and people management skills.

-
Excellent planning, organisational, and problem-solving abilities.

-
High levels of accountability and ownership.

-
The ability to make sound decisions under pressure.

-
Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.

-
Effective communication and employee engagement capabilities.

-
A passion for continuous improvement and operational excellence.

As an MCO Operations Lead, you will drive the execution, governance, and performance management of the Electronics Material Cost Optimization (MCO) roadmap. Your work will help accelerate savings delivery, improve operational visibility, and support business performance goals.

Responsibilities

Lead the execution and governance of the Electronics Material Cost Optimization (MCO) roadmap.
Manage and maintain MCO opportunities within LearPro and Foundry to ensure data accuracy and progress visibility.
Coordinate cross-functional teams to drive implementation of cost optimization initiatives.
Monitor roadmap performance, implementation status, and savings achievement against targets.
Conduct financial booking reviews with Controllers to ensure accurate savings validation and reporting.
Own weekly, monthly, and executive-level reporting for MCO performance and key initiatives.
Identify, track, and escalate roadblocks that impact implementation timelines and financial results.
Analyze funnel performance metrics and recommend actions to improve conversion and execution velocity.
Facilitate alignment between Engineering, Purchasing, Program Management, Finance, and MCO stakeholders.
Drive accountability and follow-through to ensure timely closure of actions and escalations.

Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Telecommunications Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or equivalent experience.
5+ years of experience in automotive electronics, product engineering, cost engineering, purchasing, program management, product development, or a related field.
Strong understanding of automotive electronic products, including PCBs, semiconductors, passive components, connectors, and electromechanical systems.
Experience applying value engineering, design-to-cost, or cost optimization methodologies in a technical environment.

jobs.description:
Lear For You

Lear, a global automotive technology leader in Seating and E-Systems, enables superior in-vehicle experiences for consumers around the world. Lear’s diverse team of talented employees in 38 countries is driven by a commitment to innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. Lear is Making every drive better™ by providing the technology for safer, smarter, and more comfortable journeys. Lear, headquartered in Southfield, Michigan, serves every major automaker in the world. Further information about Lear is available at lear.com or on Twitter @LearCorporation.

Following its establishment in 2012, Plzeň has grown into our fastest-growing Engineering Development Center in Europe. The center focuses on the design and development of Lear products, including complex seating mechanisms and structures, foams, coatings, plastics, and trim components. The vision for Plzen is not to work as an internal supplier for our European business units but to develop into a leading Design and Development Center working on projects for all major European OEM customer groups from concept phase through to delivery.

As a Program Manager, you will lead cross-functional BMW programs, overseeing the planning, coordination, and continuous improvement of production and assembly processes across CKD partner plants from concept phase through SOP.

Responsibilities

- Plan, design, and coordinate process workflows to ensure efficient and robust production.

- Prepare work instructions and create complete and clear process documentation.

- Coordinate production and assembly planning with customers, suppliers, and manufacturing plants.

- Plan fixtures and production equipment in close collaboration with customers, suppliers, and manufacturing plants.

- Manage and monitor project progress, ensuring alignment with timelines, quality, and cost targets.

- Plan, design, and coordinate follow-up launches and engineering changes up to SOP (Start of Production).

- Support the technical aspects of the production process and translate BMW requirements into all CKD plants.

- Support interdisciplinary teams and actively contribute to end-to-end product development activities.

- Perform root cause analyses, define corrective actions, and ensure their implementation and effectiveness.

- Provide technical support to the Sales department during offer and quotation preparation.

- Coordinate on-site deployment dates with the customer for process approvals and re-qualifications.

- Be willing to travel to all CKD partner plants, up to approximately 5 months per year.

Experience Requirements

- Successfully completed technical education or an engineering degree (or a comparable field of study).

- Fluency in German and English (spoken and written).

- Professional experience in process management, ideally within the automotive industry.

- Strong communication skills, enabling effective collaboration with colleagues, customers, and suppliers.

- High level of self-organization, reliability, and assertiveness.

- Ability to work independently as well as effectively within a team environment.
